text: CO storage tanks was addressed by 2 development of a base case and performing a capital cost comparison vs the base case. This comparison was conditioned through a qualitative assessment of relative safety, operability, and construction considerations as summarized in Table 4.2. The base case assumed vertical pressure vessels as has been installed on the Northern Lights project in Europe. In the T-RICH application, 36 vessels would be provided and grouped into 'storage units'. In each unit, 6 vessels would be connected to each other via a common liquid inlet header, liquid outlet header, and common vapor header. Liquid CO from the plant would be distributed from the common inlet header 2 and simultaneously enter all storage vessels within the unit. Once the storage unit is filled, liquid CO will 2 be routed to the next storage unit. A total of 6 storage units were envisioned to be provided. Treating multiple vessels as a common storage unit increases the number of potential leak sources and makes construction more complex. As a result, a coarse evaluation was conducted to determine if this approach is valid, or if fewer larger units could be considered. Following this optimization a revised pre-FEED case was agreed. With both liquefaction trains producing at full capacity it would take approximately 10.2 hours to fill one unit to 90% capacity, and it would take 3 days to produce a full 20,000 m³ cargo of liquid CO (the intended capacity 2 of the dedicated CO ship). 2
